items.title: 68163_Tom Whaley oral history interview
items.q: So I went down there and made an audition for the guy and the guy says, all right, the job is yours.

ctx.x: Dan Carey, excuse me. Who couldn't read too well, and there was -- what's that guy, Walter Johnson.

Yeah, Walter Johnson. He was the greatest of them all. And there was another fellow named Skinny Johnson. Oh, he was about six feet two or something, and when he played he'd wrap one leg around the other and sit down there. Oh, he could really play.
Now, what type of feeling went into it? Was it jazz or was it --
